From: Samir Shah <samir@falconhealth.ai>

Cc: Courtney Li <courtney.li@falconhealth.ai>
Date: 2027-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Eval material consignment & timeline (Falcon Health)

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the model routing examples. We'd like to move forward with a short evaluation: exchange a small subset of our de-identified clinical log dataset plus a curated prompt pack and grading testcases so we can validate end-to-end behavior on Redwood Dedicated.

High level asks from our side:
- Ephemeral access to Redwood test environment for 60 days.
- Usage limited to evaluation/testing (no production inference, no redistribution).
- Ability to run our grading scripts (we can provide Dockerized runners) and collect tokenized outputs.
- An MAP with milestones: dataset transfer, promptpack ingestion, initial sweep, quality review, decision.

I've attached a short PDF that lists data formats, redaction approach, and the timelines we're targeting. Can you confirm Redwood's constraints and suggest an MAP/close timeline? We're targeting a decision by the end of June.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync to align.

— Samir
Samir Shah
Head of ML Platform, Falcon Health
samir@falconhealth.ai

Attachment: Falcon_eval_requirements.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@falconhealth.ai>
Cc: Courtney Li <courtney.li@falconhealth.ai>
Date: 2027-04-21T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval material consignment & timeline (Falcon Health)

Samir — great to hear, and glad the demo landed.

Summary / proposed MAP (high level):
1) Agreement and access: sign a short MPA/consignment addendum that limits use to evaluation and requires purge after agreed retention (we propose 60 days after handoff).
2) Sample exchange: Falcon uploads a 10k-row de-identified sample and a ~100 prompt/testcase pack to a pre-signed S3 location we provide; Redwood ingests into an isolated bucket in our staging project.
3) Ingestion & validation (3 business days): our infra team validates schema/kv cache sizing and runs a single pass to verify no PII remnants.
4) Execution window (30 days): you run grading scripts; we provide streaming logs and token-level cost breakdowns.
5) Quality review & close (up to 14 days): joint review, give you model/config recommendations; decision/next steps.

Guardrails / constraints (must-haves from Redwood):
- Data may only be used for the evaluation in scope; no redistribution or third-party transfers.
- Access is ephemeral and audited; logs retained for 90 days and provided on request for audits.
- Customer-provided graders may run only against the staging account; we will not persist unapproved outputs beyond the retention window.
- Encryption in transit and at rest (SSE-KMS available).

I've attached a short MAP spreadsheet (Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx) with milestone dates you can edit. If this looks OK we'll send a one-page addendum for signature (DocuSign) and provide the upload credentials.

Next steps I propose:
- You review/mark edits in the MAP spreadsheet by Thu 4/23.
- We circulate one-page addendum for signature.
- Kickoff call to walk ingestion / grading flow (15–30 min) once signed.

Would you like Redwood to host the grading runner or will Falcon provide the Dockerized runner? If you provide the runner we can schedule an on-call window for integration.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (206) 555-0148

Attachment: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (Excel, 28KB)

From: Samir Shah <samir@falconhealth.ai>

Cc: Courtney Li <courtney.li@falconhealth.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval material consignment & timeline (Falcon Health)

Thanks Vanessa — the proposed flow is reasonable. A couple quick clarifications before we mark up the MAP: 

- KMS: we will need the S3 objects encrypted with a customer-provided KMS key (Falcon KMS) or an HSM-backed key; is Redwood able to support bringing our key for the staging bucket?
- Grading runner: we'll provide a Dockerized runner (Python 3.11, minimal system deps). Will Redwood allow network egress from the runner for fetching runtime dependencies, or is the runner executed in-air-gapped staging? If egress is blocked we can vendor-bake dependencies.
- Outputs: we want a hashed output bundle and the raw token-level outputs (for diagnostic only). Please confirm how Redwood stores those — ephemeral only?

Also attaching a short FAQ on compliance items we expect (Falcon_eval_requirements.pdf). We aim to sign quickly once we align on KMS and runner execution model.

Samir — looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (infra) to confirm the KMS/runner details and finalize the one‑page addendum. Quick answers while Laura/Karthik jump in:

- KMS: We can support customer-provided KMS keys for the staging bucket via a cross-account KMS grant. Karthik, can you confirm the steps (I believe it's a grant + our infra config).
- Runner network: by default the staging runners we provide allow limited egress (package index and telemetry endpoints). If Falcon prefers fully air-gapped execution we can support that for the trial but will need dependencies baked into the image; Karthik will help size the compute.
- Outputs: Redwood will persist raw token outputs in the staging bucket for the duration of the evaluation window (60 days) and then purge per the addendum; we can provide hashed bundles on demand. Audit logs for model calls will be available in the Console for 90 days.

Next steps (action items):
1) I will update the MAP spreadsheet with the agreed retention and add the KMS/runner options and send the one‑page addendum via DocuSign (link below).
2) Please mark edits in the MAP by EOD 4/23.
3) Once signed we'll send you a pre-signed S3 upload + an S3 ingestion checklist.

DocuSign (one-pager): https://docusign.net/sign/Redwood-FH-MPA-20270421
MAP (editable): Attached (Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx)

I'll schedule a 20-minute kickoff for Monday 4/26 (tentative) to walk ingestion. If Falcon wants to provide the runner we'll add an infra integration slot for Karthik.

— Vanessa
